The note's issue date is 26 September 2021, taken from DLA Piper ('which was issued on 26 September 2021'; --check FOUND). issues: The regulator's name is incomplete. The authority is the 'Comissão Nacional de Proteção de Dados Pessoais' according to both DLA Piper's authority tab and Data Protection Africa (both --check FOUND). The record drops 'Pessoais'.

The regulator is anachronistic next to the 2001 law. The CNPD's responsibilities were set by a separate 2013 law (Law No. 42 of 2013, per Data Protection Africa). The original 2001 law left oversight to the National Assembly (see the global-1 verdict on the Cabo Verde event). The note now says this.

Several claims in the note had no quote behind them: the European model, the constitutional habeas data remedy and Convention 108. All are confirmed by Data Protection Africa and by INAI's Convention 108 note, and quotes have been added. The primary law text (AFAPDP copy) confirms 'Lei nº 133/V/2001, de 22 de Janeiro' and its approval by the Assembly on 20 December 2000.
DLA Piper attaches 'of 22 January 2001' to Law 132/V/2001, but Law 133/V/2001 carries the same date, as the law text shows.

The coordinates (14.933, -23.5133) are central Praia, which is acceptable under the capital-city rule. For consistency, the matching event record was moved in global-1 to the National Assembly building (14.9061, -23.5154).

fieldFixes.note: Africa's first comprehensive data-protection statute: Law No. 133/V/2001 of 22 January 2001, approved by the National Assembly on 20 December 2000 and closely modelled on European (Portuguese) law. The Constitution also provides a habeas data remedy. The law was amended in 2013 and 2021, and a 2013 law set out the responsibilities of the national commission (CNPD). Cabo Verde later acceded to Council of Europe Convention 108.
